inferred_requirements.title: Password Reset Session Invalidation
inferred_requirements.description: Trigger invalidation of active user sessions upon a successful password reset event.
inferred_requirements.justification: Directly stated in the prompt requirement: 'Implement password reset session invalidation'.

inferred_requirements.title: Refresh Token Blacklisting Across Clusters
inferred_requirements.description: Blacklist active refresh tokens across all deployment clusters upon session invalidation triggered by password reset.
inferred_requirements.justification: Directly stated in the prompt requirement: 'blacklists active refresh tokens across all clusters'.

inferred_requirements.title: Distributed Token Revocation Propagation
inferred_requirements.description: Revocation lists or states must synchronize or be queryable across all independent clusters with bounded propagation latency.
inferred_requirements.justification: Why 1: Without cross-cluster synchronization, a refresh token invalidated in Cluster A could still be accepted in Cluster B. Why 2: A distributed caching layer, centralized database check, or pub/sub revocation broadcast mechanism is required to enforce global invalidation. Why 3: Revocation status must achieve eventual consistency across all compute boundaries within an acceptable security window.

inferred_requirements.title: Token Identifier Uniqueness and Extraction
inferred_requirements.description: Refresh tokens or their unique cryptographic identifiers (JTI) must be extractable and matched against the revocation blacklist during authentication verification.
inferred_requirements.justification: Why 1: Blacklisting entire tokens requires a reliable identifier to prevent unbounded memory usage or imprecise matching. Why 2: The authentication middleware must parse the token identifier and perform an O(1) or O(log N) lookup against the blacklist store. Why 3: Any validly signed refresh token whose identifier appears in the blacklist must be rejected unconditionally.

inferred_requirements.title: Token Storage Mechanism and Protocol Standards
inferred_requirements.description: The specific data store (e.g., Redis cluster, SQL database) and token format standards (e.g., JWT, opaque tokens) are unstated.
inferred_requirements.justification: The prompt does not specify the underlying datastore topology or whether tokens are structured JWTs or opaque references.

inferred_requirements.title: Cross-Cluster Sync Latency and Consistency Model
inferred_requirements.description: The exact acceptable replication lag or consistency model (e.g., strong vs. eventual consistency) for multi-cluster sync is unstated.
inferred_requirements.justification: The prompt mandates cross-cluster blacklisting but does not define maximum allowable propagation latency SLA.
